reranked_evidence.title: Police clash with youth-led Cockroach Janta Party protesters in New Delh - The Jerusalem Post
reranked_evidence.snippet: ## The months-old movement and the planned protest are seen as the biggest public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term in office, drawing millions of supporters. A police officer monitors CCTV footage from a mobile command-and-control vehicle at the Jantar Mantar protest site, where CJP supporters have gathered ahead of a planned march to Parliament on the opening day of the Monsoon Session, demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Supporters of India's youth-led "cockroach" movement were caned by police on Monday as they sought to march on parliament in the capital, New Delhi, despite authorities denying permission for the protest. A police decision to forcibly move hunger-striking activist Sonam Wangchuk to hospital on Saturday has galvanized the movement, with thousands of supporters arriving through the night at the protest site of Jantar Mantar in the heart of New Delhi for the march on the opening day of parliament's monsoon session.

reranked_evidence.title: ‘Won’t back down’: Indian student protesters return after police crackdown - Al Jazeera
reranked_evidence.snippet: *More than 100 students injured in police action against thousands of demonstrators during march on parliament. The heart of New Delhi – Parliament Street and Connaught Place, a colonial-era square – bears the imprint of Monday’s police crackdown on thousands of protesters, most of them students, who had shut down the capital, demanding that Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resign. After dark on Monday, Abhijeet Dipke – the leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a political pressure group that called the march – returned to a torn-down stage at the CJP’s main protest site near Jantar Mantar, an 18th-century observatory that is now an important location for protests. This is where more than 100 protesters from student unions have been sleeping for nearly a month to join Sonam Wangchuk, a prominent activist, on a hunger strike to seek the minister’s resignation.

reranked_evidence.title: Mossad says it foiled Iranian plot to infiltrate Israel, attack senior officials - The Times of Israel
reranked_evidence.snippet: ## French criminal Turut Ozkor, who went by ‘Philip,’ was allegedly recruited to gather intel on a target in Israel and carry out an attack, and was subsequently expelled by Paris. Working with foreign intelligence services, Israel foiled an Iranian plot to send operatives into Israel to harm senior Israeli officials, the Mossad intelligence agency said in a statement on Thursday. The effort, led by Iran’s Intelligence Ministry, involved turning to criminal organizations, who would in turn recruit people inside Israel or who could enter Israel for gathering intelligence on a target, then carrying out an attack. Oskhari was killed in Israel’s 12-day bombing campaign against Iran in 2025 and was a key figure in plots to attack Jewish and Israeli targets worldwide, said the Mossad. reranked_evidence.title: Why political fury is boiling over on the streets on India’s capital - CNN
reranked_evidence.snippet: Security personnel use batons to disperse protesters during a march towards Parliament on July 20, 2026 in New Delhi, India. For days the streets and parks in the center of India’s capital have seethed with the biggest demonstrations it has seen in years as young protesters demand change to a national exam system they say cheats millions of them out of a fair chance. Earlier this week, as the mostly Gen-Z protesters tried the bring their demands to the parliament building at the heart of the world’s biggest democracy, they were met with tear gas and police violence, struck with the bamboo sticks officers carry in lieu of batons. A police personnel fires tear gas shells to disperse activists and supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) during a protest demanding the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged NEET examination irregularities in New Delhi on July 20, 2026. Injuries sustained by a protester are seen during a demonstration led by the CJP campaign at Jantar Mantar on July 21, 2026, in New Delhi, India.

reranked_evidence.title: ‘It becomes inevitable’: the toxic mix fuelling deadly political violence around world - The Guardian
reranked_evidence.snippet: After killing of a British former MP, experts say dehumanising rhetoric, declining institutional trust and disinformation fuelling a global problem. On 9 July, the body of Ann Widdecombe, an uncompromising, staunchly conservative former UK government minister turned TV personality and spokesperson for the radical-right Reform UK party, was found at her home in south-west England. Ten years after the murder of the Labour MP Jo Cox by a far-right extremist**,** five years after a Conservative MP, David Amess, was stabbed to death by a supporter of Islamic State,and as MPs from across the political spectrum report on a tide of abuse and threats, the killing has reignited the UK’s debate on political violence. Attacks against elected officials across the political spectrum are rising not just in Britain but across the west, with experts saying that ever more dehumanising rhetoric, declining institutional trust and widespread disinformation are combining to create a growing problem.

reranked_evidence.title: Iran expands media crackdown with cases against 300 citizens - The Jerusalem Post
reranked_evidence.snippet: # Iran opens files against 300 people accused of speaking to diaspora media, judiciary announces. ## The move comes weeks after Iranian authorities issued indictments against dissident media groups, alleging they had encouraged the nationwide protests in January. Iran’s judiciary has opened files against 300 Iranians accused of speaking with Iran International, the Manoto Network, or individuals affiliated with the two diaspora media sites, the judiciary reported on Saturday. “Investigations into these individuals have been placed on our agenda, indictments have been issued against them, and the cases of these 300 people have been referred to Branch 15 of the Tehran Islamic Revolutionary Court.”. The charges were said to include intelligence cooperation with the enemy; espionage for the enemy during wartime; moharebeh (waging war against God); efsad fel-arz (corruption on earth); encouraging and inciting people to violence and killing; destruction of public property; financing terrorism; propaganda activities against the people, against the Islamic system, and against Islam, in cooperation with the Zionist regime and the United States; and efforts to undermine and weaken Iran. Several weeks ago, Iranian authorities indicted dissident media groups, alleging they had encouraged the nationwide protests in January.

reranked_evidence.title: IDF, Shin Bet kill Hamas commander who held multiple Israeli hostages - The Jerusalem Post
reranked_evidence.snippet: # IDF, Shin Bet kill senior Hamas Oct. 7 commander who held several Gaza hostages captive. ## Nasman held several former hostages, including Romi Gonen, Emily Damari, Ziv and Gali Berman, Eitan Mor, Matan Angrest, and Omri Miran. The IDF and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) killed Adham Ibrahim Sha'aban Nasman, Hamas's Gaza City Brigade Operations Head, over the weekend, the two announced in a joint statement on Tuesday morning. He also held several former hostages captive, including Romi Gonen, Emily Damari, Ziv and Gali Berman, Eitan Mor, Matan Angrest, and Omri Miran. In addition, the IDF and Shin Bet noted that Nasman held a number of senior Hamas positions, including serving as the intelligence officer of the Gaza City Brigade and the commander of the Al-Shati Battalion. Recently, Nasman attempted to train terrorists from Hamas' Gaza City Brigade and worked to advance the production and distribution of weapons to the brigade's battalions.

reranked_evidence.title: Iran hangs six accused of membership in banned group, as executions ramp up amid war - The Times of Israel
reranked_evidence.snippet: ## Vahid Baniamerian, 34, hanged alongside five others over alleged ties to People’s Mujahedeen of Iran; in prison outside country, inmates protest drug-related executions. Baniamerian, a 34-year-old academic who taught physics, was sentenced to death along with five other defendants on charges of membership of the outlawed People’s Mujahedeen of Iran (MEK) organization. He is one of dozens of people that rights groups say are political prisoners Iran has executed since the war with the United States and Israel started, from protesters to alleged members of banned groups and people convicted of spying. Iran has pressed ahead with executions since the earliest phase of the war finished in March, in what activists see as an attempt to instill fear in society and prevent a repeat of the protests that shook the leadership earlier this year. “With the breakdown of the ceasefire and the resumption of the war, we are deeply concerned that the authorities will exploit the situation to intensify the execution of political prisoners,” said Mahmood Amiry-Moghaddam, the director of the Iran Human Rights (IHR) NGO, which tracks executions.

reranked_evidence.title: ‘I started cursing him in Arabic’: Ex-hostage reveals words to Hamas captor upon release - The Times of Israel
reranked_evidence.snippet: Hostage Rimon Buchshtab-Kirscht speaks to her Hamas captor as she's being released to the Red Cross in Gaza, November 28, 2023. In her first long-form interview more than two years after her release from captivity, freed hostage Rimon Buchshtab-Kirscht shared this week what she told her Hamas captor as she was handed off to Red Cross personnel in Gaza. Buchshtab-Kirscht was 36 when she was abducted by the Hamas terror group during its October 7, 2023, onslaught, and then returned to Israel as part of a hostage-prisoner exchange and ceasefire deal that November. She was referring to her husband Yagev Buchshtab, who was kidnapped alongside her from their home in Kibbutz Nirim and then killed in captivity. She added, “And then the terrorists in the car gave me a speech about going out.” She recounted that they told her, in English: “Smile and wave.” She continued: “And when you go out to that audience, who are barking and raging and screaming at you, they start telling you, ‘Don’t be afraid.’”.
